items.title: 11th HSF Kramer-NLU Delhi International Negotiation Competition: LIVE UPDATES
items.summary: National Law University (NLU) Delhi will be hosting the 11th edition of the HSF Kramer-NLU Delhi International Negotiation Competition (INC) beginning today. Organised jointly by Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer (HSF Kramer) and NLU Delhi, the competition has been held since 2014. This year's edition runs from August 21 to 23 at the University's campus in Sector-14, Dwarka. 38 teams from law schools around the world are expected to take part. Each university fields one team of two students. Participants will step into the roles of international lawyers, negotiating a series of legal problems modelled on real-life situations. Each round will be judged by a panel that includes renowned lawyers and academicians. The competition consists of two preliminary rounds followed by knock-out advanced rounds. The two advanced-round winners will then face off in the final. Today's proceedings begin at 3 PM with registration and penalty appeals of Negotiation Plans for Preliminary Rounds, followed by the inaugural ceremony, opening ceremony, and a panel discussion titled Practitioners' Masterclass on M&A. items.title: The cost of India’s AI data centre boom | LME 157 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: Let’s say an AI data centre is coming to your neighbourhood, it’s easy to feel like you’ve been chosen for the future. Like the Avengers just set up Headquarters next door. But then you look at the cost. Enormous amounts of electricity. Millions of litres of water. Hundreds of acres of land. And surprisingly few jobs. New York, Texas, Virginia These are all states in the US that are shutting down data centres An estimate by Tech Radar says in just the first three months of 2026, $130 billion worth of date centre projects have been blocked or delayed across the US. And a Reuters-Ipsos poll in June found something interesting. A majority of Americans did not oppose data centres in general. But 59 percent said they did not want one built within ten miles of their home. In other words, people may like the idea of AI. They just don't necessarily want the infrastructure in their backyard. And here is the strange part. While other countries and communities are asking questions, India is competing to attract more data centres. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.
